lectures.title: The Cholas: rulers, conquests, administration and culture

items: **Imperial Cholas:** c. 9th-13th CE; key association of the period: Rajendra Chola.
**Founder:** **Vijayalaya** (Vijayalaya Chola) established the Chola Empire in the 9th century; he captured Tanjavur.
**Later Chola capital:** Gangaikondacholapuram, the later imperial capital; the capital shift Tanjore → Gangaikondacholapuram belongs to the Later Cholas.
**Thanjavur:** associated with the Brihadeshwara Temple / Chola architecture (Chola → Thanjavur).

parts.t: Early rulers and the Battle of Takkolam
items: **Aditya I:** defeated Pallava Aparajita; expanded north.
**Parantaka I:** defeated Pandyas & Sri Lanka; lost Thakkolam (949) to the Rashtrakutas.
Takkolam → Rajaditya → Krishna III; Chola → Rashtrakuta link: Battle of Thakkolam, 949
**Commemoration of the Battle of Thakkolam (949 CE):** Rajaditya Cholan RTC, Thakkolam, renamed in memory of Prince Rajaditya Chola.
**Accession:** Rajaraja-I came to the throne in 985; beginning of the golden era of the Chola Empire.
**Rajaraja Chola I (985-1014 CE):** major imperial expansion; administrative expansion.
**Temple:** Brihadisvara / Brihadeeswara / Peruvudaiyar Temple, Thanjavur, constructed by Rajaraja Chola I, 1010 CE.
**Sri Lanka:** captured northern Sri Lanka, destroyed Anuradhapura.
**Navy:** first Chola king credited in source with creating a Naval Army.
**Rajendra I / Rajendra Chola I (11th c. CE; 1014-1044 CE):** Ganga expedition; naval expansion; Chola Gangam; overseas expeditions.
**Title:** **Gangaikonda Chola**, taken after the northern / Ganga campaign (Rajendra → Gangaikonda).
**Gangaikonda Cholapuram:** built by Rajendra I, c. 1035 CE.
**Chola Gangam / Ponneri artificial lake:** huge artificial lake built by Rajendra Chola I to commemorate the victory over the rulers of the Ganga region.
**Sri Lanka:** captured the southern island, completing the conquest of Ceylon; defeated Mahinda V.
**Srivijaya:** 1025 CE naval expedition against Kadaram + Srivijaya.

parts.t: Kulottunga I and the last ruler
items: **Kulottunga I (11th-12th c. CE; 1070-1122 CE):** abolished tolls; Chola administration and overseas commercial links.
**Kulottunga I and Sri Lanka:** gave complete freedom to Sri Lanka; married his daughter to a Sinhala prince.
**Maritime network:** Sri Lanka → Malay Peninsula → Sumatra → Southeast Asia.
Very large villages administered as a single unit (Taniyur ≠ Brahmin village)
**Village administration (levels):** Mandalam → Kottam / Valanadu → Nadu → Ur.
General Chola terms for tax / revenue
Land whose revenue was set apart for maintenance of village tanks (Eripatti → village tank)
**Tank irrigation:** associated with the Cholas; a major feature of the agricultural economy.
**Uttaramerur inscription:** dynasty Chola; famous for village administration.
**Includes:** Sabha; village assemblies; local committees; committee selection / working.
**Thanjavur inscription:** ruler Rajaraja I; records his military achievements, the defeat of the Chera naval force at Kandallur; also reflects Chola overseas expansion.
**Recall:** Thanjavur → Rajaraja I → Chera naval defeat.
**Rajaraja I + Rajendra I:** temple-wall inscriptions that recorded victories and achievements.
**Why Chola history is well documented:** extensive temple-wall inscriptions, an unusually rich historical record (the major reason).
**Architecture:** Dravida style → monumental temples → cultural centres.
**Religion / arts:** Shaivism + temple institutions → music + dance + festivals.

lectures.title: The Hoysalas: capital, rulers, temples and style

items: **Capital:** **Dwarasamudra** → present-day Halebidu, Hassan district, Karnataka (capital PYQ: Dwarasamudra → Halebidu).
Hoysaleshwara construction associated with his reign
Hoysala territories were absorbed into the emerging Vijayanagara sphere after Ballala III's death (1343 CE)
**Hastimalla:** Kannada poet and playwright at the court of the Hoysala rulers; Kannada literary contribution.
**Dynasty:** Yadava Dynasty of Devagiri = a medieval South Indian dynasty.
**Geographical identity:** Western India / Deccan, centred on Devagiri.
**Period:** 12th century → early 14th century; the Yadavas ruled around 1187-1317 AD in western India.
**Initial status:** initially ruled as feudatories of the Western Chalukyas.
**Rudrama Devi link:** Kakatiya Rudrama Devi defeated the Seuna rulers of Devagiri.

lectures.title: The Kakatiyas: rulers, capitals, wars and inscriptions

items: **Dynasty:** Kakatiya Dynasty; region: Eastern Deccan; period: 12th-14th centuries CE (Kakatiyas = 12th-14th c.).
**First mention of the Kakatiyas:** the **Magallu inscription**, issued by Danarnava, mentions the Kakatiyas for the first time.
**Religion of the early kings:** the early Kakatiya kings patronised Jainism; Bethanamathya also patronised Jainism.
**Capital shift:** the Kakatiya capital was shifted from Hanamakonda to Warangal during the reign of Ganapatideva (1254).
**Orugallu:** known as the abode of drama artists / actors (from Kridabhiraman).
**Warangal Fort:** Prola Raju-II built the Swayambhu Devalayam & Kesavalayam inside it.

parts.t: Early rulers: Betha Raju, Prola Raju, Durga Nripathi
items: **Betha Raju-II:** built Setti, Kete & Kesari Samudram; Kesari Samudram was named after his royal title Vikrama Kesari.
**Prola Raju-II:** built the Swayambhu Devalayam & Kesavala, dedicated to Lord Shiva.
**Durga Nripathi:** succeeded his father Betha Raju II; mentioned in the Kazipet inscription.
**Rudra Deva:** ascended the throne after Prola Raju in 1158 AD; built the Thousand-Pillar Temple.
**Mahadeva:** ascended the throne after Rudra Deva, 1196 (after Rudradeva → Mahadeva).
**Ganapatideva (Ganapati Dev):** Kakatiya ruler; father of Rudrama Devi.
**Contribution:** shifted the capital to Warangal (1254); expanded up to Kanchi.
**Muthukur Battle (1263):** between the Kakatiya forces of Ganapatideva (allied with Manmasiddhi II) and the Pandyan king Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I.
**Rudramba / Rudramadevi:** daughter of Ganapati Dev; immediate successor of Kakati Ganapatideva; ascended the throne after Ganapathi Deva in 1260.
**Female ruler:** Rudrama Devi → Kakatiya; the 4th independent ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty.
**Military link:** Rudrama Devi defeated the Pandyas of South Tamil Nadu + the Eastern Ganga rulers of Orissa + the Seuna rulers of Devagiri.
**Yadava conflict:** Kakatiya ↔ Seuna / Yadava of Devagiri.
**Marco Polo:** visited Motupalli port / Andhra Desa during Rudramadevi's (Rudramba's) rule.
**Rudrama** = 4th independent ruler + defeated Pandyas, Eastern Gangas & Seunas.

parts.t: Pratapa Rudra and the Sultanate invasions
items: **Pratapa Rudra:** succeeded his grandmother Rudrama Devi; ascended the throne in 1296.
**First sultanate invasion on the Kakatiyas:** Alauddin Khilji.
**Death of Pratapa Rudra:** the Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka inscription says Pratapa Rudra died jumping into the Narmada.
**Recharla Rudra:** built the Ramappa Temple; title: Kakatiya Stapanacharya.
**Jayapa Senani:** author of Nrittaratnavali; profession: Gaja Sahini.
**Ambadeva:** the Tripuranthakam inscription records the victorious achievements of Amba Deva.
Narrates Rudra Deva as Vinaya Bhushan
Pratapa Rudra died jumping into Narmada

lectures.title: The Kakatiyas: administration, economy, temples and literature

items: Collective name of all Kakatiya administration departments
Holds supreme authority over all departments
Advisor to the king in Judiciary
Officials who enjoyed land without any cess / tax; Number = 12
Official who levies taxes based on the assessment given by the Karanam
**Mada:** Kakatiya gold coins were known as Mada.
**Nishkam, Tankam & Varaha:** gold coins in currency in the Kakatiya period.
**Samayamu:** caste associations during the Kakatiya period.
**Women's property inheritance:** wholly by daughters & daughter's daughters (mentioned in Vignanesvaram of Ketana).
**Motupalli:** Kakatiya seaport, the most important port-town; associated with exports, imports, customs and Marco Polo (Kakatiya port → Motupalli).
**Ganapathi Deva Abhaya inscription:** issued by Ganapatideva; found at Motupalli.
**Marco Polo:** visited Motupalli port during the Kakatiya (Rudramadevi) period.
**Motupalli epigraph:** concerns trade + tariff rates; gives information on exports / imports (Motupalli → port trade → commodity tariff).
**Commodities include:** sandal; camphor; rose water; ivory; pearls; corals; copper; zinc; lead; silk; pepper; areca nuts.
The Motupalli epigraph is evidence of **imports and exports through Motupalli port**.
**Cloths:** the chief export of the Kakatiyas (chief exporter of cloths).
**Large irrigation tanks:** associated with the Kakatiyas; agricultural expansion and water management.
Jagadala Mummadi (son of Bayyana Nayaka, minister of Ganapathi Deva)
Built across the Munneru river basin in Warangal
Kesari Samudram named after his royal title Vikrama Kesari
Built by Recharla Rudra (1213 AD); example of Ekasila architecture
Kakatiya Dynasty (built in 1163 CE by Rudradeva / Prataparudra I)
Built by Prola Raju-II; dedicated to Lord Shiva
**Jalakaranda:** musical instrument mentioned in the Dharmasagar / Dharmasagaram inscription.
**Ketana:** earned the title **Abhinava Dandi** by rendering Dasakumara Charitham into Telugu (Abhinava Dandi → Ketana).

lectures.title: The Reddis of Addanki and Kondaveedu

items: **Founder:** **Prolaya Vema Reddy** founded the Reddy Kingdom (1324).
**Kondaveedu:** associated with the Reddy kingdom (Reddy → Kondaveedu).
**Capital shift:** Anapota Reddy shifted the capital from Addanki to Kondaveedu (Manyamapura inscription of Anapota Reddy).
**Titles:** Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu; Mlecchabdhi Kumbodbhava; Rachur Durgavibhala.
**Kapaya Nayaka's court:** Prolaya Vema Reddy served in Kapaya Nayaka's court (Anitalli Kaluva Cheru inscription of Anitalli).
**Reign:** Prolaya Vema Reddy ruled till 1353 (Mani Kesavara inscription).

**Steps to Pathala Ganga (Srisailam) & Ahobilam:** he built the stepped stone pathways (Sopanamargas) to make the sacred pilgrimage shrines of Ahobilam and the perilous Pathala Ganga descent at the Srisailam Mallikarjuna temple.
**Mutnuri inscription:** steps to Pathala Ganga (Srisailam) completed in 1346.
**Court poet:** Errana, the last poet of Kavitrayam.
Shifted capital from Addanki to Kondaveedu
Built Veera Siro Mandapam (Srisailam), for Shaivite devotees who offered their own limbs or heads (Siro-karthanam) to Lord Mallikarjuna
Occupied the throne after Anavema Reddy, 1386; title Karpura Vasanta Rayalu; expert in Bharata Natya; wrote Vasantarajeeyam (Vasantha Rajeeyam)
Title Sarvagna; great poet; Reddy king skilled in music
**Surambika:** queen of Pedakomati Vema Reddy; excavated the Santana Sagaram tank.
**Santhana Sagaram inscription:** author Srinatha; related to the tank by Surambika (queen of Pedakomati Vema).
**Last Reddy kings:** Racha Vema Reddy was the last ruler of Kondaveedu; Veera Bhadra Reddy of Rajahmundry was the last Reddy king.
Prolaya Vema Reddy served in Kapaya Nayaka's court
Capital shifted from Addanki to Kondaveedu by Anapota Reddy
Steps to Pathala Ganga (Srisailam) completed in 1346
Related to tank by Surambika (queen of Pedakomati Vema)
**Srinatha:** served as educational officer in the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy.
**Veerasaivism:** the popular religion of the Reddy period.
**Motupalli (Reddy):** important port; occupied by Mallaya Reddy; Somaya issued 'Abhaya Sasana' for trade development.
**Tippayya Setti / Avachi Tippayya:** famous for overseas trade during the Reddy period; Srinatha dedicated Haravilasam to him.
**Haravilasam (by Srinatha):** literary work of the Reddy period giving information on sea-borne trade; describes imports & exports.
**Errana:** last poet of Kavitrayam (Kavi Traya); court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddy.
**Works:** Narasimha Puranam; Telugu translation of the Mahabharata: the later part of Aranya Parvam.
**Honours:** defeated Dindima Bhattu (court poet of Devaraya-II); honoured with Ganda Penderam.
**Works:** Haravilasam / Haravilasamu, Srungara Naishadham, Palnati Veera Charitra, Kasikhandam, Bhimakhandam, etc.

parts.t: Royal authors, court poets and music
items: Sangeeta Chintamani (work on music); Sahitya Chintamani; Srungara Deepika & Saptasati Charita; Saptha Sathi Saara Teeka
**Vamana Bhanu Bhattu** (court poet of Pedakomati Vema)
Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam, Usha Parinayam, etc.
Andhra Bhagavatam, Narayana Satakam, Bogini Dandakam, Veera Bhadra Vijayam
**Potana:** of the Reddy period; contemporary of Pedakomati Vema Reddy & Srinatha.
**Music works:** Sangeeta Chintamani (Pedakomati Vema) + Sangita-Sudhakaram (Singa Bhupala II).

corrections.title: The Yadavas (Seunas) of Devagiri
corrections.rocket: Period: 12th century → mid-14th century / Chronology: Yadavas ruled around 1187–1317 AD in western India
corrections.corrected: Period: 12th century → early 14th century; the Yadavas ruled around 1187-1317 AD in western India.
corrections.checked: Seuna sovereign rule c. 1187-1317; Harapaladeva was defeated in 1317, which is the early, not the mid, 14th century (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seuna_(Yadava)_dynasty)

corrections.title: The Kakatiyas: administration, economy, temples and literature
corrections.rocket: Pakala Tank - Rudra (army officer of Ganapathi Deva) - Built across the Munneru river basin in Warangal
corrections.corrected: Pakala Tank: built by Jagadala Mummadi (son of Bayyana Nayaka, minister of Ganapathi Deva); built across the Munneru river basin in Warangal.
corrections.checked: The Pakhal inscription names Jagadala Mummadi, son of Bayyana-Nayaka, a minister of the Kakatiya king Ganapati, as builder (Epigraphia Indica record, https://jainqq.org/pagetext/Epigraphia_Indica_Vol_12/032566/230; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakhal_Lake). Recharla Rudra is the builder of Ramappa, not Pakala.

corrections.title: The Reddis of Addanki and Kondaveedu
corrections.corrected: Last Reddy kings: Racha Vema Reddy was the last ruler of Kondaveedu; Veera Bhadra Reddy of Rajahmundry was the last Reddy king.
corrections.checked: Racha Vema Reddy (1420-1424) was the last ruler of Kondavidu and Veerabhadra Reddy (1423-1448) of Rajahmundry the ninth and last Reddi king; no king 'Vasanta Raju' ends the line (Vasantaraya is a title of Kumaragiri Reddy) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reddi_Kingdom; https://www.indianetzone.com/27/history_reddi_community.htm)
